name: Hermanus and the Overberg
tagline: The world's best land-based whale watching, on a cliff path above a bay filled with southern right whales, with great white sharks, penguins and the southern tip of Africa within reach.
highlight: A southern right whale mother and calf just metres from the cliff path, seen with no boat needed.
shortDescription: A seaside town 90 minutes from Cape Town with whales from June to November, plus shark-cage diving at Gansbaai, Cape Agulhas, wine in the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley and coastal walks.
metaDescription: A Hermanus and Overberg travel guide: whale watching from the cliff path, Walker Bay, Gansbaai shark diving, Cape Agulhas, De Hoop, Hemel-en-Aarde wine, penguins at Betty's Bay, best time and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Whale watching, coastal cliffs, sharks, wine, southernmost tip of Africa
goodFor: Whales, coastal walks, wine, a day trip or weekend from Cape Town

image.file: File:HER - Breaching southern right whale near Hermanus, South Africa, 2017.jpg
image.alt: A southern right whale breaching out of the water near Hermanus

intro: Hermanus, a seaside town on Walker Bay, about 120 km east of Cape Town, is regarded as one of the best places in the world to see whales from land. From about June to November, southern right whales come into the shallow waters of the bay to mate and give birth, and they can be seen just a few metres from the rocks along a 12-km cliff path that runs along the shore. Whale watching is at its best in September and October.

The town has a long tradition of whale-watching. A 'whale crier', dressed in traditional costume, blows a kelp horn to tell visitors where whales have been sighted, and each September the town holds a Whale Festival. Away from the sea, Hermanus has a pleasant old harbour, craft shops and restaurants, and the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, a cool-climate wine region known for pinot noir and chardonnay, is close by.

The wider Overberg region has more to offer. Gansbaai, the great white shark capital of the world, offers shark-cage diving, Cape Agulhas marks the southernmost tip of Africa, De Hoop Nature Reserve has dunes and whales, and Betty's Bay has a colony of African penguins. It makes a good weekend from Cape Town, or a stop on the way to the Garden Route.

whyVisit.intro: Hermanus offers easy, close whale watching, and a coast full of wildlife.

attractionsIntro: Hermanus is compact, and the surrounding region has several excursions.

attractions.name: The Hermanus Cliff Path

image.file: File:HER - Southern right whale showing its fluke near Hermanus, South Africa, 2017.jpg
image.alt: A southern right whale lifting its tail flukes near the rocky shore of Hermanus

attractions.text: A 12-km walking path along the sea cliffs, with viewing platforms where whales can be seen very close to shore, plus rock pools and fynbos.
attractions.tip: Walk between the Old Harbour and Grotto Beach.

attractions.name: Voëlklip and Grotto beaches

image.alt: Voëlklip Beach with its curved sands and mountains behind

attractions.text: Sandy beaches on Walker Bay, backed by mountains, good for walks and views of the whales.
attractions.tip: Swim at Grotto Beach in summer.

attractions.name: The Old Harbour and Whale Crier
attractions.text: A small historic harbour with a museum, and the whale crier, who announces sightings with a kelp horn.

attractions.name: Gansbaai and Shark Alley

image.alt: A great white shark swimming underwater

attractions.text: A fishing town about 40 km east, where boats take visitors to see great white sharks from cages or from the deck. It is a controversial activity, and operators differ.

attractions.name: Cape Agulhas

image.file: File:AGU - Rocky shoreline at the southern tip of Africa, Cape Agulhas, 2017.jpg
image.alt: The rocky shoreline at Cape Agulhas, the southernmost point of Africa

attractions.text: The southernmost tip of Africa, marked by a plaque, where the Indian and Atlantic Oceans meet, with a historic lighthouse.

attractions.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
attractions.text: A cool-climate wine valley near Hermanus, producing some of South Africa's best pinot noir and chardonnay.

thingsToDoIntro: Whales, walks and wine make up the days.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the cliff path
thingsToDo.text: Look for whales from the rocks.

thingsToDo.title: Take a whale-watching boat trip
thingsToDo.text: Licensed boats go out from the harbour, and stay a respectful distance.

thingsToDo.title: See African penguins at Stony Point
thingsToDo.text: A colony at Betty's Bay, between Cape Town and Hermanus.

thingsToDo.title: Attend the Whale Festival
thingsToDo.text: A September festival with music and food.

foodIntro: Hermanus's food is seafood and local produce, with wine to match.

areas.text: Hotels and guesthouses facing the bay.

gettingThere.intro: Hermanus is about 120 km from Cape Town.

options.text: About 1.5 hours via the N2 and R43, or a scenic coastal route via Clarence Drive.

gettingAround.intro: The town is walkable, and a car is best for the wider area.

bestTime.headline: September–October for whales
bestTime.summary: Hermanus has a Mediterranean climate, with mild, wet winters and dry summers.

seasons.text: Warm and dry, but no whales.
Whales arrive, with cool, wet weather.

bestTime.avoid: Whale watching outside June to November.

days.title: Whales
days.morning: Drive from Cape Town via Clarence Drive.
days.afternoon: The cliff path and the Old Harbour.

days.title: Sharks or wine
days.morning: Shark diving at Gansbaai, or a boat trip.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you see the whales.
tips: Go in September or October for the most whales.
Walk the cliff path in the morning, when the sea is calm.
Book boat trips and shark dives in advance.
Do not approach whales in the water.
Book accommodation ahead for the Whale Festival.

faq.q: When is the best time to see whales?
faq.a: June to November, with September and October the peak.
No. Whales can be seen from the cliff path.

Can I visit as a day trip?
faq.a: Yes, though a night lets you enjoy the evening.
Operators follow safety rules, but it is a controversial activity, so choose carefully.
